name: Mini abdominoplasty

card.summary: A smaller tummy tuck that removes excess skin and tightens tissue below the navel, used to flatten a lower-abdomen bulge when liposuction alone is not enough and a full abdominoplasty would be too much.
card.note: Surgery under anaesthesia; seroma, infection, scarring and delayed healing are documented complications.

quick.overview:
Mini abdominoplasty is a limited tummy tuck for people whose excess skin and muscle looseness sit mainly below the navel. A smaller incision is used than in a full abdominoplasty, and the procedure is often combined with liposuction to contour the area, giving a flatter lower abdomen.

The 1987 description of the procedure in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery reported a series of 14 patients, and defined it as correcting limited lower abdominal musculofascial relaxation and fat deposition when suction alone is insufficient and a full abdominoplasty is too much. A 2004 review described combining it with aggressive truncal liposuction as a 'marriage' technique for limited scars.
quick.how: It is a surgical procedure performed by a plastic surgeon under anaesthesia, usually with a smaller scar and, in published descriptions, a quicker return to activity than a full abdominoplasty. Surgeons assess skin excess, fat and muscle laxity to decide between liposuction, mini or full abdominoplasty.
quick.risks: Abdominoplasty overall is described as generally safe in qualified hands but with higher complication rates than many cosmetic procedures. Documented complications include seroma, hematoma, infection, delayed healing, tissue necrosis, scarring, sensation changes, asymmetry and blood clots. Smoking, obesity, diabetes and prior abdominal surgery are risk factors.

lead: Mini abdominoplasty, or mini tummy tuck, is a reduced form of abdominoplasty aimed at excess skin and fat in the lower abdomen, below the navel [1][2]. It uses a smaller incision than a full abdominoplasty and, in the classic form, does not require moving the navel [3].

For appearance, it is used by people with a lower-abdominal bulge or skin laxity, commonly after pregnancy or weight loss, who want a flatter lower abdomen. Gym forum members mention a mini tummy tuck as the option for loose lower-belly skin that diet and exercise do not change [4][5].
Surgical literature describes it as a middle option between liposuction and full abdominoplasty, often combined with liposuction [2][6].

chain: Excess lower-abdomen skin and tissue removed or tightened
Often combined with liposuction for contour
Flatter lower abdomen with a short scar
angle.text: The surgery physically removes lower-abdominal skin excess and tightens tissue, giving a flatter profile that diet and training cannot change when loose skin is the cause.

infobox: Faster than full abdominoplasty per authors' reports; gym restrictions during healing

paras: A 1987 report describes the procedure for patients whose deformity lies below the semicircular line, correcting limited lower musculofascial relaxation and fat when liposuction alone is insufficient and a full abdominoplasty is too much [3]. A 1997 paper describes a tumescent version [7].

In 'marriage' abdominoplasty, aggressive truncal liposuction is combined with a modified mini-abdominoplasty to treat lower skin excess, muscle laxity and fat with limited scars; the authors said it applied to over half of patients seeking abdominal contouring [6].

Modern abdominoplasty was popularised in the late 1960s, with Pitanguy among those associated with the technique, and liposuction introduced by Illouz in 1983 changed how abdominal contouring was done; liposuction was initially paired with mini-abdominoplasty [2].

Evidence consists of surgical case series and reviews. The 1987 series of 14 patients described indications, technique, course and complications [3]. The 2004 review reported excellent contour improvement and a more rapid return to activity than full abdominoplasty in the authors' experience [6]. Reviews of abdominoplasty technique cover classification by skin, fat and muscle layer and treatment levels [8]. A randomized trial of local anaesthetic infiltration compared analgesics in fleur-de-lys abdominoplasty, a different variant [9].

Wikipedia reports abdominoplasty has higher complication rates than many cosmetic procedures; seroma is among the most common, with hematoma, infection, delayed healing, necrosis, scarring, sensation change, asymmetry and venous thromboembolism also reported. Risk factors include smoking, obesity, diabetes, prior abdominal surgery and combined procedures [1].

A T Nation member reported a surgeon advising a minimum of two months without gym work after abdominoplasty, while a powerlifter was told two to three weeks until some exercise resumed; these are anecdotes [10][11].

timeline.event: Pitanguy popularises abdominoplasty for aesthetic improvement [2].
Mini-abdominoplasty described in a series of 14 patients [3].

lore.intro: Gym forums mention the mini tummy tuck mainly as an option for loose skin after weight loss [4][5].

claims.claim: Loose skin below the navel cannot be fixed by diet or exercise, only by surgery
claims.believers: A T Nation reply says a mini tummy tuck is the route for excess skin at that point [4].
claims.experts: Surgical literature describes mini-abdominoplasty for limited lower deformity not corrected by suction alone [3].
